events.title: Citrix NetScaler ADC & NetScaler Gateway Authentication Bypass and Memory Overflow Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-19489 & CVE-2026-19490)
events.summary: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway devices have two critical vulnerabilities—a memory overflow and an authentication bypass—first observed on 9 September 2026.
events.why_it_matters: The vulnerabilities carry high CVSS scores of 8.8 and 9.3, and CVE-2026-19490 is listed in the KEV, indicating potential active exploitation. Defenders should prioritize patching affected Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway devices.

reasons: Australian research lab Triskele Labs reported the vulnerability.
Record indicates an Australian source identified the issue.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2026-19490 as exploited in the wild, added 2026-09-09, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2026-09-12.
CVE-2026-19490 is rated 9.3 (critical) under CVSS 4.0 by the CNA that assigned it, the highest of the 2 scored CVEs here.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-19490 being exploited in the next 30 days at 23%, the highest of the 2 CVEs here.

events.title: Credentialed Pre-Port Discovery: Don't Probe the Host, Ask it
events.summary: If your scan engine already holds credentials for a host, it can ask that host which ports are open instead of probing for them. Every scan begins with the same question: which ports on this host are open? Everything after it, from identifying services to checking for vulnerabilities to evaluating policy, depends on the answer being right. The traditional answer comes from the outside: the scan engine sends traffic to a range of ports and infers each port's state from how the host responds.
